intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years. Walk across Sultanahmet Square to the stunning Blue Mosque, admiring its six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context on Byzantine and Ottoman history.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food and Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Continue to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Interact with vendors, taste free samples, and soak in centuries of trading culture in a single morning.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local kitchen where you'll learn to prepare classic Ottoman and Turkish dishes such as börek, meze, lamb kebabs, and baklava. Classes typically include a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients, followed by a communal meal with your instructor and fellow travelers.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury, view priceless relics including the Prophet Muhammad's cloak and sword, and tour the Harem quarters to understand the private lives of sultans and their court. The palace overlooks the Bosphorus, offering breathtaking views.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Street Food Evening
experiences.description: Board a public ferry or small private boat for a scenic Bosphorus cruise at sunset, passing between Europe and Asia while viewing Ottoman palaces, fortresses, and waterfront mansions (yalıs). After docking, explore the Karaköy waterfront for an authentic street food evening — try balık ekmek (fish sandwiches), simit, midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and çay (Turkish tea) from local vendors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the Havaist airport bus or metro to the city center (budget-friendly option ~50-80 TRY vs expensive taxis). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a 24-hour simit (sesame bread ring) cart or a nearby döner kebab shop near the hotel for under 80 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival simple. Pre-download offline maps (Google Maps or Maps.me) for Istanbul. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport kiosk or use ATMs for Turkish Lira. Avoid unofficial taxi touts at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. After a slow start, head to the nearest local bakery or simit cart for a classic Turkish breakfast. Then explore the beachfront area around the hotel on foot, getting oriented with the neighborhood, local shops, and nearby transport connections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take public transport (bus or metro) into the Sultanahmet historic district — the heart of old Istanbul. Visit the iconic Hagia Sophia (free entry for the mosque sections), one of the world's greatest architectural wonders, a former Byzantine cathedral turned Ottoman mosque. Walk the surrounding plaza and admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Sultanahmet area at dusk when the mosques are beautifully lit. Visit the Hippodrome of Constantinople (now Sultanahmet Square) — free to walk through. Head back toward the hotel and explore a local neighborhood restaurant for your first proper Turkish dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local simit cart or bakery near hotel — simit with tea costs under 30 TRY
meals.lunch: Cheap pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a local pide salonu in Sultanahmet for around 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Neighborhood lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) near hotel — a full meal with soup, main, and bread for 100-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Get an Istanbulkart (rechargeable transit card) from any metro station kiosk — saves significant money on all public transport. Dress modestly when visiting mosques (cover shoulders and knees; women bring a headscarf).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Topkapi Palace — the grand seat of the Ottoman Empire for centuries. The main palace grounds have an entrance fee (~250 TRY) but offer incredible history and views of the Bosphorus. Explore the Imperial Council Hall, Treasury courtyards, and lush gardens. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill from Topkapi to the Gülhane Park (free) — one of Istanbul's oldest and most beautiful public parks, especially lovely in May with spring flowers. Then explore the nearby Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex (~100 TRY), housing one of the world's great collections of ancient artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Eminönü waterfront district. Watch the famous Galata Bridge fishermen casting lines at sunset. Buy a fresh balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from one of the iconic floating boats or waterfront stalls — a legendary Istanbul street food experience for around 60-80 TRY.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a traditional Turkish breakfast spread at a local café — menemen (egg dish), olives, cheese, tomatoes, tea for ~80-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from a local market or a quick börek (savory pastry) from a street vendor near Topkapi for 40-60 TRY
meals.dinner: Balık ekmek fish sandwich at Eminönü waterfront + a cup of çay (tea) from a nearby çay bahçesi (tea garden) for under 100 TRY total

day_by_day.notes: The Topkapi Harem section costs extra (~150 TRY additional) — skip if on a tight budget as the main palace is already impressive. Museum Pass Istanbul can save money if you plan to visit many paid museums — worth calculating based on your itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets, completely free to enter. Wander through over 4,000 shops selling carpets, spices, jewelry, ceramics, and leather goods. Practice bargaining and enjoy the sensory overload of colors and sounds. Best to go early before it gets too crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar / Mısır Çarşısı) — another incredible market focused on spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, and teas. Free to enter. Buy local spices or snacks as affordable souvenirs. Explore the lively streets of Eminönü and Tahtakale surrounding both bazaars.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot (free, great views) to the Karaköy neighborhood on the European north side. Explore the trendy-yet-affordable Karaköy district. Visit the historic Galata Tower exterior (beautiful to photograph at night). Enjoy dinner in Karaköy's local eateries.

meals.breakfast: Simit, boiled egg, and çay from a street cart near the Grand Bazaar for under 40 TRY
meals.lunch: Kuru fasulye (slow-cooked white beans) with rice and bread at a lokanta inside or near the Grand Bazaar — a filling classic for ~80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Lahmacun (thin Turkish pizza with minced meat) and ayran (yogurt drink) at a local Karaköy restaurant for ~80-120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Do not feel pressured to buy anything in the bazaars. Shopkeepers are persistent but friendly — a polite 'hayır teşekkürler' (no thank you) works well. Keep your belongings secure in crowded market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most magnificent Ottoman mosque, built by the legendary architect Sinan for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. Free to enter. The complex sits on a hilltop in the old city with panoramic views. Explore the surrounding mosque complex including the tombs of Suleiman and his wife Hürrem Sultan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Beyazıt neighborhood and the historic Istanbul University area. Visit the Beyazıt Mosque (one of Istanbul's oldest Ottoman mosques, free). Browse the famous second-hand book market at Sahaflar Çarşısı (Old Book Bazaar) adjacent to the Grand Bazaar — fascinating for history lovers even if you don't buy anything.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Fatih district — a deeply traditional and authentic Istanbul neighborhood. Explore the Fatih Mosque complex at sunset. Stroll through local streets far from tourist crowds and experience everyday Istanbul life. Have dinner at a no-frills neighborhood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at a local kahvaltı salonu (breakfast restaurant) near the hotel — full spread for ~100-130 TRY
meals.lunch: Mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and bread at a simple lokanta near Süleymaniye for ~60-80 TRY
meals.dinner: Kuzu tandır (slow-roasted lamb) or köfte (meatballs) at a Fatih neighborhood restaurant for ~120-160 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Süleymaniye area has several excellent budget tea houses with rooftop views — perfect for a mid-morning çay break with stunning Golden Horn vistas. Look for the Çay Bahçesi near the mosque walls.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to Üsküdar on the Asian side of Istanbul — one of the best and most affordable Bosphorus experiences (~15 TRY with Istanbulkart). Enjoy stunning views of the skyline, Topkapi Palace, and the Bosphorus strait during the 20-minute crossing. Explore the charming, authentic Üsküdar neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) from the outside — the iconic small tower in the Bosphorus is a symbol of Istanbul. Walk along the Üsküdar waterfront promenade. Explore the Çamlıca Hill area (accessible by bus) for the best panoramic views of Istanbul spanning both continents — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side by ferry and explore the Kadıköy district on the Asian side first if time permits (take a separate ferry) — a lively, youthful neighborhood with fantastic street food and markets. Otherwise return to European Istanbul for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Simit and tea on the ferry or at the Eminönü waterfront before boarding — under 40 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh fish at a simple balık lokantası (fish restaurant) in Üsküdar waterfront — grilled fish plate with salad and bread for ~120-150 TRY
meals.dinner: Kadıköy street food tour — try kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and fresh juice for ~100 TRY total

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's great budget pleasures — the views are spectacular and cost almost nothing. Ferries run frequently throughout the day. Kadıköy is especially lively in the evening with locals — a great authentic experience away from tourist areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — one of the finest examples of Byzantine art in the world, with stunning 14th-century mosaics and frescoes. Modest entrance fee (~100 TRY). The surrounding Balat and Fener neighborhoods are among Istanbul's most historically rich and photogenic areas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring Balat — Istanbul's historic Jewish quarter, now a colorful, bohemian neighborhood with rainbow-painted houses, antique shops, and street art. Wander through narrow cobblestone streets, visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople (free to visit), and explore the Greek Orthodox Fener neighborhood next door.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Golden Horn waterfront back toward the city center. Visit the Pierre Loti Hill (accessible by cable car ~30 TRY round trip) for sunset views over the Golden Horn — one of Istanbul's most romantic and budget-friendly viewpoints. Named after the French novelist who loved Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery in Edirnekapı neighborhood — fresh börek and tea for ~50-70 TRY
meals.lunch: Meyhane-style lunch in Balat — small plates of mezze (hummus, ezme, cacık) with bread at a casual restaurant for ~100-130 TRY
meals.dinner: Pide at a neighborhood pide fırını (pide oven restaurant) near Pierre Loti or back near the hotel for ~80-120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Balat is a photographer's paradise — bring your camera. The neighborhood is gentrifying but still very affordable and authentic. Wear comfortable shoes as the streets are steep and cobblestoned. The area around Fener and Balat is best explored slowly on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Beyoğlu district and the famous İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's main pedestrian boulevard stretching from Taksim Square to the Galata area. Ride the historic Tünel funicular (one of the world's oldest underground railways, ~15 TRY). Browse bookshops, music stores, and small galleries along the avenue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pera Museum (~100 TRY) — a superb private museum in Beyoğlu with excellent collections of Orientalist paintings, Anatolian weights and measures, and Kütahya tiles. Particularly famous for housing Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer.' Then explore the atmospheric backstreets of Galata and Cihangir neighborhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the vibrant nightlife atmosphere of Beyoğlu without spending much — walk through Asmalımescit and Nevizade streets lined with meyhanes (Turkish taverns). Enjoy the lively street atmosphere. Have dinner at one of the many affordable restaurants in the area.

meals.breakfast: Pastane (pastry shop) on İstiklal Avenue — fresh croissant or poğaça (savory pastry) with Turkish tea for ~50-70 TRY
meals.lunch: Döner wrap from a local döner shop on or near İstiklal for ~80-100 TRY — filling and delicious
meals.dinner: Meze and grilled meat at a neighborhood meyhane in Asmalımescit — order carefully to stay within budget, around 150-200 TRY with a soft drink

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is pedestrian-only except for the historic red tram that runs its length (free to watch, ~15 TRY to ride). Beyoğlu has excellent free street entertainment especially on weekends. The Cihangir neighborhood has a lovely bohemian café culture — great for a budget coffee break.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a group of car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara, a short ferry ride from Istanbul. Take the IDO ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı (~50-80 TRY each way). Visit Büyükada, the largest island, with beautiful Victorian-era mansions, horse-drawn carriages, and peaceful pine forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle on Büyükada (~100-150 TRY for a few hours) and cycle around the island — the best way to explore. Visit the hilltop Aya Yorgi (St. George) Monastery with panoramic sea views. Enjoy the peaceful, traffic-free atmosphere that feels worlds away from Istanbul's chaos.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon/early evening. Enjoy the sunset views of the Istanbul skyline from the ferry deck. Have dinner back in the city at a local restaurant near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the ferry terminal or bring packed snacks for the ferry — simit and fruit for ~40-50 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — grilled fish with salad and bread for ~150-180 TRY (slightly pricier on the island but worth it)
meals.dinner: Simple ev yemeği (home cooking) at a lokanta near the hotel — soup, main dish, and dessert for ~120-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands are incredibly popular on weekends — consider visiting on a weekday if possible. Check ferry schedules in advance as they vary seasonally. The islands are perfect for a relaxed day away from city noise. No cars are allowed on the islands — only horses, bicycles, and electric vehicles.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) in Sultanahmet — a breathtaking underground Byzantine cistern with 336 marble columns, atmospheric lighting, and mysterious Medusa head bases. Entrance fee (~250 TRY) but absolutely worth it for history lovers. Then visit the nearby Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) with stunning Byzantine floor mosaics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arasta Bazaar — a quieter, less touristy alternative to the Grand Bazaar, located right behind the Blue Mosque. Browse handmade ceramics, textiles, and crafts at more relaxed prices. Then finally enter the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) — free to enter during non-prayer times, with its stunning interior of 20,000 İznik tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Sound and Light Show at the Sultanahmet Square (free, seasonal — check local listings). Enjoy the magical atmosphere of the illuminated mosques and historical square at night. Have a final evening stroll through the Sultanahmet area.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at a Sultanahmet area café — full spread with eggs, cheeses, olives, tomatoes for ~100-130 TRY
meals.lunch: Tantuni (spiced meat wrap) from a street vendor near Sultanahmet for ~60-80 TRY
meals.dinner: Kebab dinner at a no-frills Sultanahmet area kebapçı — Adana or Urfa kebab with rice, salad, and bread for ~120-160 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque is closed to tourists during the five daily prayer times — check the prayer schedule before visiting (roughly 5-6 times per day, each closure lasts about 90 minutes). The Basilica Cistern is cool underground — bring a light layer. Photography is allowed inside both attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) in Karaköy — Turkey's first modern and contemporary art museum with excellent rotating exhibitions (~200 TRY). Located in a beautiful building with Bosphorus views. Then walk through the Tophane neighborhood and explore the Tophane-i Amire (Ottoman cannon foundry) complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a public Bosphorus ferry cruise — not the expensive tourist boats but the regular IDO/BUDO commuter ferries that travel up the Bosphorus for a fraction of the price (~25-40 TRY with Istanbulkart). Travel from Eminönü toward Sarıyer or Beykoz for stunning views of Ottoman palaces, yalıs (wooden waterfront mansions), and the Bosphorus bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ortaköy neighborhood in the evening — a charming waterfront village beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Famous for its kumpir (loaded baked potatoes) — a must-try Istanbul street food for ~80-120 TRY. Browse the weekend craft market (if applicable). Enjoy the atmospheric waterfront square with the beautiful Ortaköy Mosque backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local Karaköy café for ~80-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Packed snacks for the ferry — buy fresh fruit, nuts, and simit from Eminönü vendors before boarding for ~50 TRY
meals.dinner: Kumpir (loaded baked potato) in Ortaköy — a legendary Istanbul street food experience for ~100-150 TRY with toppings

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's greatest budget secrets — tourists pay 10x more for the same views on tourist boats. The Ortaköy area can get crowded on weekends but the atmosphere is fantastic. The Bosphorus Bridge is beautifully lit at night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the European Bosphorus shore, where Atatürk spent his final days. Guided tours are required (entrance ~350 TRY for main sections). The palace has 285 rooms, 46 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier. Arrive early as timed entry tickets sell out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to the Beşiktaş neighborhood — a lively, authentic Istanbul district popular with locals. Explore the Beşiktaş market area and the fish market. Visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi, ~80 TRY) with fascinating Ottoman naval history and imperial caiques (royal rowing boats). Explore the waterfront Barbaros Hayreddin Paşa Park.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Nişantaşı neighborhood for window shopping and people-watching — Istanbul's upscale fashion district is beautiful to walk through even on a budget. Then head back toward your area for a final relaxed dinner. Consider trying a traditional Turkish dessert parlor (muhallebici) for künefe or kazandibi.

meals.breakfast: Açık büfe (open buffet) at a local hotel café or a full Turkish breakfast spread at a Beşiktaş neighborhood café for ~100-120 TRY
meals.lunch: Balık sandwich (fish sandwich) from the Beşiktaş fish market waterfront — fresh and delicious for ~70-90 TRY
meals.dinner: Neighborhood lokanta near the hotel — a comforting full meal with soup, main course, salad, and dessert for ~130-160 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires purchasing tickets in advance if possible — the palace has strict visitor number limits. The Harem section costs extra. Photography is not allowed inside the palace. The palace grounds and exterior are magnificent even from outside.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning revisiting your favorite neighborhood or any missed spots. Consider a leisurely breakfast at a traditional kahvaltı salonu (Turkish breakfast restaurant) — a proper send-off with the full spread of cheeses, olives, eggs, honey, clotted cream, tomatoes, cucumbers, and unlimited tea. Visit any last-minute souvenir shops — best budget options include the Spice Bazaar for spices and Turkish delight, or Arasta Bazaar for ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at the hotel if your flight allows for extra afternoon time. Take a final walk along the Bosphorus or beachfront area near the hotel. Head to the airport with plenty of time — use the Havaist bus or metro (most budget-friendly option) from the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Istanbul with incredible memories of 13 days exploring one of the world's greatest cities. The journey to the airport takes 45-90 minutes depending on traffic — factor this into your departure timing.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell Turkish breakfast at a local kahvaltı salonu — the full spread with unlimited tea for ~130-160 TRY — treat yourself on your last morning
meals.lunch: Quick and easy — a final döner kebab or lahmacun wrap from a street vendor for ~80-100 TRY before heading to the airport
meals.dinner: Airport food or on the plane — grab a final Turkish tea at the airport for a proper goodbye to Istanbul

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport procedures at Istanbul Airport. The Havaist bus to the airport costs ~100-120 TRY and runs frequently — much cheaper than taxis (~400-600 TRY). Consider buying extra Turkish delight, spices, or apple tea as affordable, lightweight souvenirs. Keep some TRY for airport expenses or exchange remaining currency before departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel bar or a nearby 24-hour lokanta (Turkish diner) close to the resort — try a simple menemen (Turkish egg dish) or a simit with cheese.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-arrange airport transfer to avoid taxi confusion late at night. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront promenade near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings and enjoy the sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby local bazaar or neighborhood market to sample Turkish street food and get a feel for local life. Browse fresh produce, spices, and handcrafted goods. If the resort is near the European side, head toward Kadıköy or the nearest historic district for a casual stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a waterfront fish restaurant near the resort for a classic Istanbul seafood dinner. Try grilled sea bass (levrek) or sea bream (çipura) with meze starters.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Turkish classics like olives, white cheese, tomatoes, cucumbers, honey, and fresh bread.
meals.lunch: Street food near the local bazaar — try a balık ekmek (fish sandwich) or a gözleme (savory stuffed flatbread) from a street vendor (budget-friendly, ~$5–8).
meals.dinner: Mid-range waterfront fish restaurant near the beachfront — expect to spend ~$20–30 per person including meze and a soft drink.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to adjust to the time zone. Pick up a local SIM card or activate an eSIM for easy navigation throughout the trip. Download offline maps of Istanbul.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Sultanahmet — the historic heart of Istanbul. Start with the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya), one of the world's greatest architectural achievements. Arrive early (opens at 09:00) to beat the crowds. Marvel at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and Ottoman additions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — admire the stunning interior with 20,000 Iznik tiles and six minarets. Then explore Sultanahmet Square and the ancient Hippodrome, including the Serpent Column and Egyptian Obelisk. Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — an atmospheric underground Byzantine cistern.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet at dusk. Enjoy dinner in the neighborhood with views of the illuminated mosques.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — a legendary lokanta serving authentic köfte (meatballs) with bread and ayran. Very affordable (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant or a similar mid-range Ottoman cuisine restaurant in Sultanahmet — try Ottoman-inspired dishes like lamb with dried fruits and pilaf (~$25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia is free to enter but requires modest dress (cover shoulders and knees). The Blue Mosque is free but may be closed during prayer times — check the schedule. Comfortable walking shoes are essential today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace — the grand seat of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem, and the stunning palace courtyards with panoramic Bosphorus views. Book tickets online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Gülhane Park — Istanbul's oldest public park, located just below Topkapi. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri), a world-class complex housing the Alexander Sarcophagus and artifacts spanning 5,000 years of civilization.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Grand Bazaar area for an evening stroll (note: the bazaar itself closes around 19:00 on weekdays). Explore the surrounding streets of Beyazıt and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace — a historic eatery with Ottoman recipes and Bosphorus views (~$15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Beyazıt area — try a traditional Turkish pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a local pideci restaurant (~$10–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is large — wear comfortable shoes and allocate at least 3–4 hours. The Harem requires a separate ticket. Closed on Tuesdays — adjust schedule if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Browse carpets, ceramics, jewelry, spices, and textiles. Practice your bargaining skills! Opens at 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü — a sensory feast of spices, dried fruits, Turkish delight, and local delicacies. Cross the Galata Bridge on foot and enjoy views of fishermen and the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul at sunset. Explore the bohemian Galata and Karaköy neighborhoods below.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and delicious lunch at a traditional lokanta near the Grand Bazaar — try a set lunch menu with soup, main course, and salad (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Karaköy neighborhood — try Karaköy Lokantası or a similar mid-range restaurant known for modern Turkish cuisine (~$20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Budget for souvenir shopping — set a limit to avoid overspending. The Spice Bazaar is a great place to buy Turkish tea, spices, and lokum (Turkish delight) as gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry across the Bosphorus to Üsküdar on the Asian side of Istanbul — a short and scenic 20-minute ride. Explore the charming Üsküdar neighborhood, visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, and walk along the Asian waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kadıköy — Istanbul's most vibrant and youthful neighborhood on the Asian side. Explore the famous Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı), packed with gourmet food shops, fresh produce, delis, and street food. Browse the eclectic shops and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the ferry back to the European side at sunset for stunning Bosphorus views. Enjoy dinner in the Karaköy or Galata area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Kadıköy Market food tour — graze on various street foods including kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and fresh börek (~$10–15 total).
meals.dinner: Karaköy or Galata — try a meyhane (traditional Turkish tavern) for a meze-heavy dinner with raki (Turkish anise spirit) if desired (~$25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets are very affordable (use an Istanbulkart transit card for best rates). The Asian side offers a more local, less touristy experience. Kadıköy is especially lively on weekend afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Visit İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard in Beyoğlu. Walk its entire length, ride the historic Tünel funicular, and explore the side streets (pasajlar) with their art galleries, vintage shops, and cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pera neighborhood — visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) featuring Ottoman-era paintings and the famous 'The Tortoise Trainer' by Osman Hamdi Bey. Then wander through the charming Çukurcuma antique district.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Turkish hammam (bath) experience at a historic bathhouse such as Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Tarihi Galatasaray Hamamı — a quintessential Istanbul cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast on İstiklal Avenue — try a Turkish breakfast spread (serpme kahvaltı) at a local café (~$10–15).
meals.lunch: İstiklal side streets — try a classic döner kebab wrap or a lahmacun (thin Turkish flatbread with minced meat) from a local eatery (~$5–10).
meals.dinner: Post-hammam dinner in Beyoğlu — try Zübeyir Ocakbaşı for excellent grilled meats and kebabs in a lively atmosphere (~$20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hammam costs range from $30–60 per person for the full experience including scrub and massage — book in advance. İstiklal Avenue is very crowded on weekends — go early for a more relaxed experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus cruise — book a public ferry tour (2-hour or full-day option) that sails up the Bosphorus strait, passing by Ottoman-era waterfront mansions (yalılar), Rumeli Fortress, and the second Bosphorus Bridge. A highlight of any Istanbul visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı (the final stop on the full Bosphorus tour) — a charming fishing village on the Asian shore. Hike up to the medieval Yoros Castle for spectacular views of where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Istanbul. Enjoy a relaxing evening near the waterfront in Beşiktaş or Ortaköy neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant in Anadolu Kavağı — try grilled fish with salad and bread (~$15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Ortaköy neighborhood — famous for its kumpir (loaded baked potatoes) as a street food snack, followed by dinner at a mid-range restaurant overlooking the Bosphorus and the iconic Ortaköy Mosque (~$20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (Şehir Hatları) is very affordable (~$5–10 for the full route). Private tour boats are more expensive but offer commentary. Check ferry schedules in advance as they are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus. Tour the ceremonial halls, crystal staircase, and the room where Atatürk passed away. Book tickets in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Beşiktaş neighborhood — explore the lively market area and the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) with its impressive collection of Ottoman imperial caiques (royal rowboats) and maritime artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's fashion and dining district. Window shop along Abdi İpekçi Street and enjoy the elegant café culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş market area — try a fresh fish sandwich from the market stalls or a hearty soup at a local lokanta (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Nişantaşı — dine at a mid-range modern Turkish restaurant. Try contemporary takes on classic Anatolian dishes (~$25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires guided tours only — tours run at set times and tickets sell out, so book online. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands in the Sea of Marmara. The islands are car-free and offer a peaceful escape from the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada by bicycle or horse-drawn carriage (phaeton). Visit the historic Aya Yorgi Monastery at the hilltop for stunning sea views, and stroll through the charming Victorian-era wooden mansions.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon/early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a restaurant on Büyükada's waterfront — try grilled calamari or shrimp with salad (~$15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near Aegean Bliss Resort — try a neighborhood restaurant for classic Turkish home cooking like slow-cooked lamb or chicken güveç (clay pot stew) (~$15–20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Büyükada takes 60–90 minutes. Use your Istanbulkart for the ferry. Bicycle rentals on the island cost ~$5–10/hour. The island can be very busy on weekends — consider visiting on a weekday.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii/Museum) — a stunning Byzantine church in the Edirnekapı neighborhood featuring some of the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world. A hidden gem compared to Hagia Sophia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — Istanbul's most colorful and historic districts along the Golden Horn. Wander the rainbow-painted streets, visit the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, and browse the antique and vintage shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Pierre Loti Hill (Eyüp) for a cable car ride and panoramic views of the Golden Horn at sunset. Visit the historic Eyüp Sultan Mosque — one of Istanbul's most sacred sites.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Balat neighborhood — dine at a charming local café or bistro in one of the colorful restored buildings. Try a homemade Turkish dish of the day (~$10–15).
meals.dinner: Eyüp or Fener area — enjoy a traditional Turkish dinner at a family-run lokanta with dishes like stuffed eggplant (karnıyarık) and lentil soup (~$12–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Balat is very photogenic — bring a camera. The neighborhood has become trendy with cafés and boutiques but retains its authentic character. Wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestone and hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern (İstanbul Modern) — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum, recently relocated to a stunning new waterfront building in Karaköy. Explore rotating exhibitions of Turkish and international contemporary art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk along the Karaköy waterfront and through the hip Tophane neighborhood. Visit the Tophane-i Amire (historic Ottoman cannon foundry) and explore the neighborhood's art galleries and design studios. End the afternoon at the Egyptian Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) for last-minute shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Istanbul's best mid-range restaurants. Consider Hamdi Restaurant near Eminönü for spectacular Golden Horn views and excellent southeastern Turkish cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Splurge on a full Turkish breakfast (serpme kahvaltı) at a renowned breakfast spot in Karaköy or Beşiktaş — a leisurely spread with 20+ small dishes (~$15–20 per person).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Istanbul Modern café — enjoy a coffee and a snack with waterfront views (~$10–15).
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant or similar — try the mixed kebab platter with Turkish bread, salads, and a dessert of künefe or baklava (~$30–40 per person for a special farewell meal).

day_by_day.notes: Use this day for any remaining souvenir shopping and to revisit favorite spots. Istanbul Modern is closed on Mondays. Book the farewell dinner restaurant in advance, especially for weekend evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — enjoy a relaxed last breakfast at the hotel. Take a final stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort and soak in the sea views. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, squeeze in one last activity — visit a nearby neighborhood café for a final Turkish tea (çay) and simit, or browse a local bookshop for a Turkish coffee table book as a memento. Begin transfer to Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Istanbul. Reflect on an incredible 13-day journey through one of the world's most captivating cities.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the last of the Turkish olives, cheese, and fresh bread.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a quick stop at a café near the hotel before departure — try a Turkish tea and pastry.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for Istanbul Airport (IST) — it is one of the world's largest airports and security/immigration can take time. Pre-book your airport transfer. Keep some Turkish lira for last-minute purchases or tips.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity, and settle into your suite overlooking the water.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort — charcuterie board, Turkish mezze selection, and a glass of local Kavaklidere wine to welcome you to Istanbul

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the resort's concierge. Request early check-in preparation so your suite is fully ready upon arrival. Keep Day 1 restful to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a lavish breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant overlooking the Bosphorus. After breakfast, take a private guided tour of the Sultanahmet Historic Peninsula — visit the iconic Hagia Sophia with a knowledgeable expert who provides exclusive context on its Byzantine and Ottoman layers, avoiding the general tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) at your own pace, followed by a private walk through the ancient Hippodrome of Constantinople. Visit the Basilica Cistern with a VIP after-hours arrangement if available, marveling at its atmospheric underground columns and Medusa heads.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the charming Arasta Bazaar for artisan browsing. Dinner at Matbah Restaurant inside the Ottoman Hotel Imperial — a refined establishment serving authentic Ottoman palace cuisine in a historic setting.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast spread at the Aegean Bliss Resort terrace — simit, beyaz peynir, olives, honey, clotted cream, fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs prepared to order, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Giritli Restaurant near Sultanahmet — a celebrated spot offering a generous Aegean-inspired mezze feast with fresh seafood, paired with local wines
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant — Ottoman palace cuisine featuring dishes like hünkar beğendi (sultan's delight), lamb with dried fruits, and rose-water desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book private guided tours and Basilica Cistern VIP access through your concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Wear modest clothing for mosque visits — shoulders and knees covered. Flat, comfortable shoes recommended for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Topkapi Palace — explore the imperial treasury housing the Spoonmaker's Diamond and Topkapi Dagger, the sacred relics pavilion, and the Harem quarters with an expert guide providing rich historical narrative about the Ottoman sultans who ruled from this palace for centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Gülhane Park adjacent to the palace for a relaxing stroll. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums — a world-class complex housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Anatolian artifacts, and tiles from the Ishtar Gate of Babylon.
day_by_day.evening: Private Bosphorus sunset cruise aboard a chartered luxury yacht departing from Eminönü. Sail past the Dolmabahçe Palace waterfront, the Bosphorus Bridge, and the wooden yalı mansions lining the shores, with canapés and champagne served on deck.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace grounds — a legendary institution serving Turkish classics with panoramic views of the Golden Horn and Bosphorus
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard the private yacht or at Tuğra Restaurant at the Çırağan Palace Kempinski — an iconic setting inside a restored Ottoman palace serving refined Turkish and international cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — verify the day and book skip-the-line tickets in advance. The private yacht charter should be arranged at least 3 days ahead through the concierge. Bring a light jacket for the evening cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private tour of the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Your expert guide will lead you through hidden passages, introduce you to master craftsmen, and share the bazaar's 15th-century history. Shop for handcrafted jewelry, silk textiles, ceramics, and antiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) for a sensory feast of exotic spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and local delicacies. Then explore the nearby Rüstem Pasha Mosque — a hidden gem adorned with the most exquisite Iznik tiles in Istanbul, often overlooked by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Turkish cooking class at a premium culinary studio in the Beyoğlu district — learn to prepare classic dishes such as börek, manti (Turkish dumplings), and baklava under the guidance of a master chef.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pandeli Restaurant above the Spice Bazaar entrance — a legendary Istanbul institution since 1901, serving traditional Turkish cuisine in a stunning blue-tiled dining room
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as your dinner, paired with local wines and raki, in a convivial private setting

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is customary in the Grand Bazaar but approach it respectfully. The private cooking class typically lasts 3–4 hours including the meal. Book well in advance as premium culinary experiences fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via a private water taxi across the Bosphorus. Explore the charming Kadıköy neighborhood — a vibrant, bohemian district beloved by locals. Wander through the Kadıköy Produce Market, sampling fresh seasonal fruits, artisan cheeses, and local specialties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Moda neighborhood in Kadıköy for a leisurely walk along the waterfront promenade with stunning views back toward the European skyline. Explore independent boutiques, local art galleries, and the historic Moda Pier. Then visit the Haydarpaşa Train Station — a magnificent neo-Gothic German-designed building on the Bosphorus shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side by private water taxi at sunset. Explore the lively Karaköy neighborhood — Istanbul's artsy waterfront district. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar with Bosphorus views before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — a legendary restaurant celebrated for its extraordinary Anatolian regional cuisine, beloved by food writers and chefs worldwide
meals.dinner: Dinner at Karaköy Lokantası — a sophisticated brasserie in a beautifully restored historic space serving elevated Turkish cuisine with exceptional wines

day_by_day.notes: The Asian side of Istanbul offers a completely different, more local atmosphere than the tourist-heavy European side — a highlight for culturally curious travelers. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Kadıköy's market streets.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Dolmabahçe Palace on the European Bosphorus shore — the 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace that replaced Topkapi as the administrative center. Marvel at its 285 rooms, 44 halls, 68 toilets, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier, a gift from Queen Victoria.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Beşiktaş and Nişantaşı neighborhoods — Istanbul's answer to Paris's Marais district. Browse luxury Turkish designer boutiques, visit the Sakıp Sabancı Museum in nearby Emirgan for world-class art exhibitions, and stroll through manicured Emirgan Park.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam ritual at the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı — a 16th-century bathhouse designed by the legendary Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan. Book a private VIP session including a full body scrub, foam massage, and relaxation in the ornate marble chamber.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sunset Grill & Bar in Ulus — a premium restaurant with sweeping panoramic views of the Bosphorus and two bridges, serving international and Turkish cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nişantaşı's Nicole Restaurant — a celebrated fine-dining establishment with a creative tasting menu showcasing the best of Turkish seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for the Selamlık and Harem sections — book both in advance. The hammam experience lasts approximately 1.5–2 hours. Avoid eating a heavy meal immediately before the hammam.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a stunning archipelago in the Sea of Marmara accessible by private ferry. Arrive on Büyükada (the largest island), where motorized vehicles are banned. Hire a private horse-drawn carriage for a scenic tour of the island's Victorian-era mansions, pine forests, and hilltop Greek Orthodox monastery of Aya Yorgi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada's charming village center — browse local shops, visit the historic Splendid Palace Hotel (a belle époque landmark), and relax on a quiet beach cove. Optionally rent bicycles to explore the island's quieter southern shores.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private ferry as the sun sets over the Marmara Sea, painting the skyline in golden hues. Freshen up at the resort before a special dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Milady Restaurant on Büyükada — a charming waterfront restaurant serving fresh Marmara seafood, grilled fish, and cold mezze with island views
meals.dinner: Dinner at 360 Istanbul in Beyoğlu — a legendary rooftop restaurant and bar offering 360-degree panoramic views of Istanbul's skyline, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn, with a sophisticated international and Turkish menu

day_by_day.notes: Depart early in the morning to maximize time on the island. The private ferry charter should be arranged through the concierge. The Princes' Islands are very popular on weekends — a weekday visit is ideal for a more peaceful experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque — the grandest Ottoman mosque in Istanbul, commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent and designed by the master architect Mimar Sinan. Explore the mosque's vast courtyard, the mausoleums of Suleiman and Roxelana, and the surrounding historic külliye complex. Afterward, explore the charming Vefa neighborhood nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the world's finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes, recently restored to stunning effect. Then walk along a section of the ancient Theodosian Walls — the 5th-century fortifications that protected Constantinople for over a thousand years.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony — a deeply spiritual Sufi ritual of the Mevlevi Order, arranged at an intimate historic venue for an authentic and moving cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — Istanbul's most celebrated köfte (meatball) restaurant, a beloved institution since 1920, for a quintessentially local experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Asitane Restaurant near the Chora Church — a scholarly restaurant that has meticulously researched and recreated historic Ottoman palace recipes from 500-year-old archival sources

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church may have restricted access depending on ongoing restoration work — verify status with your concierge before visiting. The Whirling Dervishes ceremony is a profound cultural experience — maintain respectful silence and refrain from flash photography.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — housing an important collection of Orientalist paintings, Anatolian weights and measures, and Kütahya tiles. The museum's crown jewel is Osman Hamdi Bey's iconic painting 'The Tortoise Trainer.' Explore the surrounding Pera/Beyoğlu district, historically home to Istanbul's European embassies and merchants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the famous İstiklal Avenue — Istanbul's grand 19th-century pedestrian boulevard lined with historic buildings, art nouveau architecture, churches, consulates, and vibrant shops. Ride the nostalgic Tünel funicular (one of the world's oldest underground railways, dating to 1875) and explore the atmospheric Galata neighborhood, climbing to the medieval Galata Tower for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private rooftop cocktail experience at a premium Galata hotel bar. Then attend a live classical Turkish music (fasıl) performance at a historic meyhane (tavern) in the Beyoğlu district for an authentic evening of culture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Leb-i Derya Richmond in Beyoğlu — a stylish restaurant with sweeping Golden Horn views, serving contemporary Turkish cuisine with exceptional presentation
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional Beyoğlu meyhane such as Refik or Boncuk — legendary establishments serving classic rakı table culture with cold and hot mezze, fresh fish, and live fasıl music

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is pedestrianized but can be very crowded — early afternoon is more manageable. The Galata Tower has long queues; arrange skip-the-line access through your concierge. The meyhane experience is central to Istanbul's social culture — pace yourself with the rakı.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to Bursa — the first Ottoman capital, located across the Sea of Marmara. Depart by private ferry from Istanbul to Mudanya, then private transfer to Bursa. Visit the magnificent Green Mosque (Yeşil Cami) and its adjacent Green Tomb, showcasing extraordinary 15th-century Iznik tilework in stunning turquoise hues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Grand Covered Bazaar of Bursa (Kapalı Çarşı) — one of the oldest bazaars in the world, predating Istanbul's Grand Bazaar. Visit the historic Koza Han (Silk Cocoon Inn), a beautifully preserved 15th-century caravanserai at the heart of Bursa's historic silk trade. Take a cable car up Uludağ Mountain for breathtaking views over the city and Marmara Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private ferry. Rest and refresh at the resort before a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at İskender Kebabı at Kebapçı İskender in Bursa — the legendary birthplace of the famous İskender kebab (thinly sliced döner over pide bread with tomato sauce and browned butter), a dish that originated in Bursa in 1867
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — a relaxed, indulgent evening after a full day of travel

day_by_day.notes: This is a long excursion day — depart by 8:00 AM to maximize time in Bursa. The private ferry and transfers should be pre-arranged. Bursa is an underrated gem that most tourists miss — a truly rewarding off-the-beaten-path experience.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated morning for a private Turkish breakfast experience at a celebrated breakfast specialist restaurant — a beloved Istanbul tradition. Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) is an elaborate, leisurely ritual featuring dozens of small dishes including various cheeses, olives, pastries, eggs, honey, jams, and endless tea. A cultural experience in itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sakıp Sabancı Museum in Emirgan — one of Istanbul's finest private museums, housed in a stunning Bosphorus-front mansion. Explore its permanent collection of Ottoman calligraphy, paintings, and decorative arts, as well as major international temporary exhibitions. Stroll through the adjacent Emirgan Park and its famous tulip gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Private Bosphorus dinner cruise — a different experience from the sunset cruise earlier in the trip, this time focused on a gourmet dinner aboard a luxury vessel sailing under the illuminated Bosphorus bridges, past floodlit palaces and fortresses reflected in the dark water.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate Turkish breakfast at Van Kahvaltı Evi or Çakmak Kahvaltı — celebrated Istanbul breakfast institutions offering the full southeastern Turkish breakfast experience with 20+ dishes
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Sakıp Sabancı Museum café overlooking the Bosphorus
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner aboard a private luxury Bosphorus dinner cruise — multi-course Turkish and Mediterranean menu with wine pairings, live music, and panoramic night views

day_by_day.notes: Turkish breakfast is typically a 1.5–2 hour affair — embrace the leisurely pace. Book the gourmet dinner cruise at least 5 days in advance as premium vessels have limited capacity.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy the beachfront, spa facilities, or a private yoga session arranged by the concierge. This is a well-deserved rest morning after an intensive cultural itinerary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) — Turkey's leading contemporary art museum, recently reopened in a spectacular new Renzo Piano-designed building on the Karaköy waterfront. Explore its world-class collection of modern Turkish art alongside major international exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Final grand evening in Istanbul — visit the Ortaköy neighborhood, one of Istanbul's most picturesque waterfront districts, nestled beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Browse the Sunday artisan market (if applicable), then proceed to a farewell dinner at one of Istanbul's most celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at İstanbul Modern's waterfront restaurant — a stylish space with exceptional Bosphorus views and a refined contemporary Turkish menu
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Mikla Restaurant atop the Marmara Pera hotel — Chef Mehmet Gürs's celebrated New Anatolian Kitchen concept, offering a boundary-pushing tasting menu that reinterprets Turkish culinary heritage through a modern lens, with extraordinary panoramic city views

day_by_day.notes: Mikla is one of Istanbul's most acclaimed restaurants and consistently appears on international best restaurant lists — reservations must be made well in advance, ideally when first booking the trip. Request a window table for the best views.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed walk along the beachfront promenade for a final contemplative view of the Bosphorus. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping or pick up premium Turkish goods — artisan olive oil, specialty teas, lokum (Turkish delight) from Hafız Mustafa, or handcrafted ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport. Depart Istanbul with extraordinary memories of one of the world's greatest cities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — in-flight

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent breakfast at the resort — savor every last bite of the Turkish breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a café near the resort or at the airport's premium lounge
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Arrange checkout and airport transfer through the concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Istanbul Airport check-in and security, especially for international flights. Consider purchasing a curated selection of premium Turkish products as gifts — the resort concierge can recommend the best specialty shops near the hotel.
